Specimen ID: [redacted ID]

SPECIMEN INFORMATION
Specimen Type: Formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tissue
Specimen Source: Parotid gland, fine needle aspiration biopsy
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Clinical Indication: Suspected mucoepidermoid carcinoma
Relevant Clinical History: Fine needle aspiration from parotid mass showing features suggestive of salivary gland neoplasm

TEST PERFORMED
Fluorescence In Situ Hybridization (FISH) for MAML2 Gene Rearrangement

METHODOLOGY
Interphase FISH analysis was performed on 4-micron formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tissue sections using the GenProbe XR-2000 Dual Color Break Apart Probe targeting the MAML2 gene at chromosome 11q21. The probe consists of a 5' green fluorescent probe and a 3' red fluorescent probe flanking the MAML2 breakpoint region. Analysis was performed on multiple areas of the tissue section and correlated with corresponding H&E stained slides.

RESULTS

| Probe | Locus | Result | Cells Analyzed | Abnormal Cells |
|-------|-------|--------|----------------|----------------|
| MAML2 Break Apart | 11q21 | NEGATIVE | 200 | 0 (0%) |

Interpretation: No MAML2 (11q21) rearrangement detected

DETAILED FINDINGS
Interphase nuclei from multiple tissue areas showed two intact fusion signals (yellow/overlapping red-green signals) in all cells analyzed, consistent with absence of MAML2 gene rearrangement. No cells demonstrated separated red and green signals indicative of a translocation involving the MAML2 locus.

INTERPRETATION
The FISH analysis shows no evidence of MAML2 gene rearrangement in this specimen. It is important to note that a negative FISH result does not exclude the diagnosis of mucoepidermoid carcinoma (MEC), as MAML2 rearrangements are detected in approximately 55-81% of MEC cases, with higher frequencies observed in low and intermediate grade tumors. Additionally, the dual-color break-apart probe methodology cannot detect cryptic insertions or other complex rearrangements that may not result in signal separation.

The absence of MAML2 rearrangement may be seen in:
- High-grade mucoepidermoid carcinomas (more commonly negative)
- Other salivary gland neoplasms
- Technical limitations due to tissue fixation or processing

RECOMMENDATIONS
These results should be interpreted in conjunction with histopathologic findings and immunohistochemical studies. Clinical correlation is essential for accurate diagnosis. If mucoepidermoid carcinoma remains a strong diagnostic consideration based on morphology, additional molecular testing or expert consultation may be warranted.
